title: Adverse Action Explainability Pattern
description: A pattern for generating a specific, individualised, accurate reason for any adverse credit or lending decision an automated system contributes to, rather than a generic boilerplate explanation.

history.note: Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources).

problem: A complex underwriting model can produce accurate decisions while giving applicants only a generic explanation ('creditworthiness'), which prevents both the applicant and the organization itself from quickly confirming or refuting an allegation of unfair treatment.
solution: Generate the top contributing factors behind each adverse credit decision at the individual-applicant level (e.g. via a feature-attribution method appropriate to the model), translate them into plain-language reasons, and issue them as part of the adverse-action notice, retaining the underlying factor data for later review if a dispute arises.
applicability: Any automated or algorithmic system that contributes to a credit, lending, insurance-pricing, or similar consumer-facing eligibility decision.
consequences: Feature-attribution explanations for complex models are themselves an active area of methodological debate and can be misleading if not validated; generating and storing per-applicant explanations adds infrastructure cost.

citations.title: Report on Apple Card Investigation
citations.publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services

relationships.reason: Individualised, plain-language reasons are the concrete mechanism satisfying this control's notice requirement.
The pattern's output is an adverse action notice record.
